function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run manually) to finish the whole workflow.  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that you’ll need to create/overwrite in the repository.

> **⚠️ Important** – I can’t actually run `git clone`, `git add`, `git commit` or `git push` for you, but the commands below will do it for you when you run them locally.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# Make sure you have SSH access set up for GitHub
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> If you prefer HTTPS, replace the URL with `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & generate artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create or overwrite `Dockerfile` at the root of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Use the official lightweight Node.js image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why this image?*  
> `node:18-alpine` is small (~70 MB) and includes only the essentials.  
> `npm ci` guarantees a clean install from `package-lock.json`.  
> Adjust the `CMD` if your entry point is different (e.g., `index.js`).

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can keep it in a `k8s/` folder or at the repo root):

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use another registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Tip** – If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` and expose the desired port.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a file `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest \
            .

      # Push the image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What this does**  
> * On every push to `main`, it checks out the code, logs into GHCR using the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN`, builds the image, tags it with the commit SHA and `latest`, and pushes both tags.  
> * No extra secrets are required because `GITHUB_TOKEN` already has write permission to the repo’s packages.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new/updated files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
```

> If you created the `k8s/` folder, make sure to add it too (`git add k8s/`).

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After the push, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run and publish the Docker image to GHCR.

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

| Artifact | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| Dockerfile | `/Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| Kubernetes manifests | `/k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys the app with 2 replicas |
| GitHub Actions workflow | `/.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` | Builds & pushes Docker image on `main` pushes |

Feel free to tweak the image tags, registry, or deployment settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
